sentences.text: Argovisaurus is an extinct genus of ophthalmosaurian ichthyosaurs that lived in the Middle Jurassic of Switzerland. The genus contains only one known species, A. martafernandezi, which is known from a partial skeleton.
This animal was notably large compared to its relatives, with the holotype individual estimated to be between 4.5 and 6 meters long.
The mandible of the holotype specimen is approximately 125 centimeters long.
Argovisaurus was notably large compared to its relatives.
Several bones in the skull and skeleton show abnormalities that may be evidence of traumatic injuries.
The holotype specimen was discovered before 2004 by Elmar Meier in the Hauptrogenstein Formation near Auenstein, Switzerland.
Miedema et al. formally described Argovisaurus martafernandezi as a new genus and species in 2024.
The name Argovisaurus combines the Latin name for the region of discovery with the Greek word for lizard.
The species name honors paleontologist Marta Fernández for her work on marine reptiles.
Phylogenetic analyses place Argovisaurus as an early-diverging member of the Ophthalmosauria, and it belongs to the family Ophthalmosauridae.
Although phylogenetic trees place Argovisaurus basal to the strict definition of Ophthalmosauria, authors argue it should be considered a member due to morphological similarities.
Argovisaurus lived between 170.9 and 165.3 million years ago during the Bajocian to Bathonian stages.
